title: Part 5. The tripadi *Vaishnava-vandana* of the "second" Vrindavana Dasa
html:
A Bengali vandana, entitled "Third vandana" in the 1910 edition: tripadi stanzas (2–68), then payar couplets (69–150). Introduction; Gaura, Nityananda, Advaita and their families; the associates at Navadvipa; the sannyasis; the Gosvamis of Vrindavana; associates in Gauda and Orissa; Nityananda's associates; conclusion (pp. 37–55 of the 1910 edition)1

[p. 37]

Introduction

1I praise the merciful Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda, [who contain] all avataras, the refuge of all devotees.2

Raga — as one chooses.

Refrain: Sing of Sri Krishna Chaitanya-chandra and of Balarama — Nityananda — with full voice: you will pass your life happily, gain the company of Vaishnavas and never see Yama.

2The age of Kali, like a snake, has bitten all people, and the world writhes in the burning of the poison; Gauranga, the abode of virtues, by the power of the great mantra — the name "Hare Krishna Rama" — has brought it back to life.

3Above all the Vaishnavas, purifiers of the three worlds, seeing fallen and suffering souls, were moved in their hearts by compassion and, instructing [them] in Krishna, made them happy with the happiness of Krishna.

4Listen, O base man: give up false maya, hold fast, hold fast to the feet of the Vaishnavas; by the power of a Vaishnava's mercy Kala (time) cannot devour you — you will pass [it] safely.

5Keep company with Vaishnavas, look upon a Vaishnava's form, hear with your ears a Vaishnava's words; reflect and see in your mind: apart from the Thakura Vaishnava, no one else can give devotion to Hari.3

[p. 38]

6The greatness of the Vaishnavas is unknown to the world and to the Vedas, and even the gods do not grasp its essence; I am the lowest of the low, weaker than a moth — what shall I say of it with my small mouth?

7And yet, according to this strength, day and night, reflecting day after day,
I shall describe something of Sri Chaitanya, Nityananda and all the devotees with Them.

8I shall speak of my heart: towards a rasa of which I am unworthy — towards that very rasa my mind has been drawn; do not laugh at faults of sandhi and of words: Lord Janardana accepts the feeling.4

9Simple by nature, I do not know what comes before and after, and the vandana will not go in order; therefore with words I bow and beg pardon — let no one count it an offence.5

10Prostrating my body on the ground, first of all I shall bow to the feet of Shachi and Jagannatha; then I praise Vishvarupa, the Thakura, king of sannyasis, blessed by the name Sri Shankararanya.6

11With undivided devotion I praise Gaurachandra-Hari, the descent auspicious for the world: He was born in the town of Nadia to protect the dharma of the age and spread sankirtana.7

[p. 39]

The families of the Lord and of Nityananda

12With great reverence I praise Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, then I praise the divine Gadadhara: of all the Vaishnavas none is so dear [to the Lord] — he is Chaitanya's second body.8

13I praise the mother, Padmavati, and the father, Hadai Pandita, whose son is such a one — Nityananda; I praise Prabhu Nityananda, fearless, the root of bliss, who delivered all.9

14I bow to the feet of her whose name is Varuni, the abode of Ananga-manjari:
she who is Ananga-manjari is Jahnava Gosani; Varuni is her former name.10

15Falling to the ground in joy, I praise Vasu and Jahnavi, whose son is Virachandra; I shall praise Thakura Virabhadra, deep and steadfast, with whose virtues the world was filled.

16At Nilachala Gaurahari held a chief counsel in private with Nityananda;
its reason is this: that Vira Prabhu is a descent of Gauranga Himself.11

17Do not doubt this: in the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata Vrindavana Dasa wrote it;
Abhirama understood all this and, bowing, revealed it.12

[p. 40]

18Radha and Krishna in liquid form, who dwelt in Brahma's vessel, the Mother of the world abiding in the three worlds — Bhagavan Himself become water, named Ganga-devi: I praise that daughter of Nityananda.13

19The abode of Govinda's prema, named Acharya Madhava, whose body is full of the bliss of prema — with joined palms I praise his lotus feet: Ganga-devi is his wife.14

Refrain: Well done, O Gaurangachand: spreading the net of prema, You have bound the minds of living beings; by meditation on Hari's name and qualities You have made the people of the world blessed — I die, [giving myself] as Your ransom.

Madhavendra Puri, Advaita and His family

20I praise Sri Madhava Puri: having descended to earth, he revealed devotion to Vishnu;
he is the ancient original guru, a wish-tree of compassion, Mahaprabhu's first devotee.15

21I praise the lord of Shantipura, the wise Sri Advaita, whose might is like Sadashiva's: by the power of His austerity Chaitanya, brought to earth, made His descent.16

[p. 41]

22The original energy of Kailasa, I praise Sita-bhagavati, whose might equals the power of devotion: by her vow Jagannatha descended and spread prasada.17

23The dust of Sita's feet I shall praise, placing it on my head — and I shall count myself worthy of praise; I praise her dear son, Sri Achyutananda, renounced from childhood.18

The associates at Navadvipa

24My heart's desire fulfilled, I shall praise Srivasa, non-different from Narada, the best of sages; I praise Malini-devi, whom Prabhu Nityananda and Vishvambhara called "mother".19

25I praise Narayani-devi: serving Chaitanya's feet, she received the nectar of His lips; I shall praise Sri Haridasa — the manifestation of Brahma himself — who made [people] chant the name aloud.20

26I shall praise Paramananda and Pandita Jagadananda, like Sarasvati in another form;
Thakura Sri Gopinatha fell at [the Lord's] feet and offered the Lord much praise.21

27I shall praise Murari Gupta, like that very Hanuman, whose treasure of life is Raghunatha; I praise Sri Chandrashekhara, cool as the moon, then I praise Acharyaratna.22

[p. 42]

28Govinda and Garuda I shall praise with hymns: their meditation is Gaura's feet; I shall praise Mukunda Datta, maddened by Krishna's qualities, whose singing puts the kinnaras to shame.23

29I praise Vasudeva Datta, whose secret essence and greatness cannot be told: from the breeze of his body arises prema-bhakti for Krishna — what other comparison shall I give?24

30Damodara, Pitambara, Jagannatha, Shankara, Narayana — these five brothers,
free from all desires, depending on nothing, detached — I shall praise them together.25

31Famed as the Lord's maternal grandfather, Nilambara Chakravarti I shall carefully praise: surpassing the omniscient in vision, he drew up the Lord's auspicious horoscope with predictions of the future.26

32The abode of all virtues, I shall praise Pandita Rama, harmless, doing good to others;
with all my heart, body and mind I praise Gupta Narayana, placing his feet upon my head.27

33Dwelling in the town of Nadia, I praise the guru Gangadasa, with whom the Lord studied; holding a straw between my teeth, I humbly praise Vishnudasa and Sudarshana.28

[p. 43]

34Sadashiva, Vidyanidhi, Shrigarbha and Shrinidhi, Buddhimanta Khan Mahashaya,
the brahmachari Shuklambara, heirs to the treasure of prema — these six I praise.29

35Ramadasa, Kavichandra, the scribe Vijayananda, Acharya Ratneshvara I shall praise; I shall praise the generous Shridhara, whose customer was Gauranga at his stall of banana pith, bananas and banana flowers.30

36With joined palms I praise Vanamali with his son — the two who beg for the alms of devotion; then I shall praise Halayudha and Vasudeva, whose minds are wholly given to Chaitanya.31

37The vessel of Ai's mercy, I shall praise Ishana, whom Ai brought up;
Garuda and Kashishvara I shall praise next, having praised the feet of Jagadisha.32

38Gangadasa, Krishnananda, Raya Sri Mukunda I praise with special reverence; I praise Sri Vallabhacharya, whose deed bore fruit: he gave the Lord his daughter Lakshmi.33

39With devotion in my mind I shall praise Pandita Sri Sanatana, whose daughter is Vishnupriya: by the power of what austerity, by the fruit of what merit — I do not know — Mahaprabhu became his son-in-law.

[p. 44]

40With both palms joined, I praise the brahmana Kashinatha; I shall praise Acharya Vanamali, who came and arranged the match of Lakshmi-devi for her auspicious marriage with the Lord.34

The sannyasis

41I shall praise Ishvara Puri, whom the Lord accepted as guru, considering Himself lowly; I praise Keshava Bharati with deep humility — the one who made the Lord a sannyasi.

42I praise Ramachandra Puri: seeing his vehemence, the Lord gave up everything;
Sri Puri Paramananda — I praise his feet — the one called Thakura Uddhava.35

43I praise Damodara Puri, to whom Gaurahari is subject, whose manner is like Satyabhama's; Sri Nrisimhananda the sannyasi, who delights in sankirtana, I praise, [and] the wise Satyananda.36

44I praise Garuda Avadhuta, whose prema is wondrous — marvellous to see and to hear; I shall praise Sri Vishnu Puri, who composed the Vishnu-bhakti-ratnavali to deliver people.37

45I praise Vishveshvarananda, whose life is Gaurachandra; then I praise Sri Keshava Puri; I praise Anubhavananda, Bharati Sachchidananda, then I praise Manoratha Puri.38

[p. 45]

The Gosvamis of Vrindavana

46I praise Rupa and Sanatana, dwelling in Sri Vrindavana, supremely renounced, free from the world: giving up their royal posts and taking the guise of beggars, they took a water-pot and a kaupina.39

47I praise Jiva Gosani, whom all the Vaishnavas asked: "Which truth is the essence?" Having examined all the shastras, he answered: "Bhakti-yoga alone — there is nothing higher."40

48Dwelling at Sri Radha-kunda, I praise Raghunatha Dasa, who knows the inner heart of Chaitanya; then with great devotion I praise Raghava Gosani, whose play is at Govardhana.41

49I shall praise Gopala Bhatta, who lives in one place only — near Sanatana: no other talk is in his mouth — days and nights he passes happily in Govinda's name and qualities.42

50I praise Raghunatha Bhatta, maddened by love for Krishna — in Vrindavana, among the Vrajavasis: when he reads the Bhagavata, his body is overcome by prema, and a sweet voice sounds in his telling.43

51I praise Prabhu Lokanatha, who with Bhugarbha Thakura always sports in Vrindavana: seeing people in distress, always anxious at heart, he gave them the treasure of prema and made them happy.44

[p. 46]

52With devotion I praise Prabodhananda Sarasvati, abode of the highest greatness and virtues: the Sri Chaitanya-chandramrita is a book he composed; this book is the treasure and life of the devotees.45

53With a joyful mind I praise the wise Kashishvara, whom all call the famous "Bhakta"; I praise Shuddha Sarasvati, firm in devotion to Gaura's feet: beasts and birds are captive to his feeling.46

The associates in Gauda and Orissa

54I shall praise Raghavananda, in whose house Nityananda made His power known:
on the lemon tree in his garden a kadamba blossomed — all who saw it were amazed.47

55I praise the beautiful Thakura Sri Purandara, like that very Angada Thakura: a certain brahmana, taking him, received him as a guest in his house — and with all his family saw the tail.48

56I praise Kashi, the best of Mishras, whose house is in Utkala, in whose dwelling [lived] Gauraraya; Pattanayaka Vaninatha, whose life is Jagannatha, I shall praise at his feet.49

57I praise Raya Ramananda, with whom Gaurachandra discussed the characteristics of devotion; I shall praise Sri Vakreshvara: for his dancing Vishvambhara in great bliss sang kirtana.50

[p. 47]

58I shall praise Subuddhi Mishra and Sri Govindananda the brahmana, by whose mental causeway-road from Kuliya to Gauda the Lord went, rejoicing.51

59She who is the daughter of Vrishabhanu is Gadadhara Dasa: now he has revealed his name; let no one doubt: this is Gauranga's twin body — such is Gadadhara Dasa.52

60I praise Gadadhara Dasa, whose pastimes are incomparable, whose body is full of the rasa of prema; I praise Sadashiva the vaidya: by his grace a stone at once melts and becomes water.53

61I praise Shivananda Sena, who has no thought other than Chaitanya's lotus feet; I shall praise Mukunda Dasa, living in Khanda of the vaidyas, whose son is Sri Raghunandana.54

62Mukunda Dasa's devotion — Krishna's inexpressible power — is known in the world to this day: seeing a peacock feather, his eyes grew restless and he fell in confusion, overwhelmed with prema.55

63I shall praise Sri Narahari Dasa — blessed is he, I offer myself for him — in whose heart are Chaitanya's pastimes; I praise Raghunandana, like Madana in form, whose dancing enchants the world.56

[p. 48]

64I praise Raghunatha Dasa, who delights in the happiness of prema, whose mind is bound in the net of love; I praise Acharya Purandara: in the feeling of Krishna he constantly, always weeps aloud.57

65Thakura Sri Krishnadasa, living in Akaihat — peaceful, utterly without possessions;
Paramananda Pandita, Mahaprabhu's fellow student — these I praise with devotion.58

66In the highest bliss I shall praise Pandita Sri Devananda, who always reads the Bhagavata; I shall praise Acharyachandra, who knows the inner meaning of prema, whose virtues and deeds are known to the world.59

67Govinda, Madhavananda, Vasudeva Ghosha — I praise [them], three brothers, an ocean of virtues: hearing their song, Lord Vishvambhara, [surrounded by] all His associates, could not contain Himself.60

68Gadadhara Dasa and with him Vasudeva Ghosha I shall carefully praise, both: the bud of a karavi flower that was on his ear became fragrant like a lotus before the assembly.61

Refrain: Blessed are Advaita and Gaurachandra, blessed, blessed is Nityananda, blessed, blessed is the circle of devotees; blessed, blessed are the name and the qualities, blessed, blessed is sankirtana — blessed is all this in the age of Kali.

[p. 49]

Nityananda's associates

69I praise Thakura Ramadasa, foremost among devotees,
whose fame filled the world, whose manifestation is wondrous.

70A log lay there [that only] sixteen men [could lift];
he playfully lifted it with two fingers

71and, bending in a threefold curve, made a flute of it
and played sweet songs on it.62

72The cowherd boy Shridama is Abhirama Gosani,
a second Chaitanya: his greatness has no end.63

73I praise the Sudama of Vraja — Thakura Sundara,
whose might is like fire, whose form is beautiful.

74His servant seizes a tiger and brings it from the forest,
embraces it and makes it hear the name of Hari in its ear.64

75I shall praise Sri Gauridasa Pandita Thakura,
the beloved of Nityananda, full of greatness.

76Taking the Lord's command on his head, he went to Shantipura
and brought Acharya Prabhu [Advaita] to Utkala.65

77He is called Subala, the cowherd boy of Gokula;
he gives refuge to the good and is death to the wicked.

78His power of devotion to Krishna is known to the world:
because of him the godless [went to] the netherworld (?).66

79He lives in Ambika;
in his house are the Deities of Nityananda and Chaitanya.

80While the Lord was still present he manifested [these] Deities:
whoever sees these Deities, his bonds of karma are destroyed.67

[p. 50]

81With divine garlands, sandal paste, clothes and ornaments
he adorned Nitaichand.

82With great reverence I praise Uddharana Datta,
who travelled to the holy places together with Nityananda.68

83I shall carefully praise Thakura Parameshvara Dasa,
who revealed himself while dancing in kirtana:

84calling forty jackals one by one,
he made them all utter the sixteen names.69

85I praise Thakura Pippalai, artless in a child's feeling,
all of whose pastimes and play are like a child's.

86Then I praise Thakura Kamalakara Dasa,
whose highest exultation is in the sankirtana of Krishna.70

87I praise Purushottama Tirtha, the crown of rasikas,
who is intoxicated with the rasa of Sri Krishna.71

88I praise the mad, playful Kala Krishnadasa:
always beside himself with prema, he cannot keep hold of his cloth.72

89With joined palms I shall praise Sri Saranga Thakura,
in whose patched quilt there were six score snakes.73

90I praise Makaradhvaja Kara, a treasury of virtues,
who always sings Krishna's qualities in the Lord's presence.

91I praise Bhagavata Acharya, Mishra Kaviraja;
I praise Ananta Acharya, [who lives] in Navadvipa.74

92Then I shall praise the feet of Madhu Pandita,
whom all call the Vaishnava Pandita.75

[p. 51]

Associates in Orissa and others

93I shall praise the feet of Govinda Acharya,
who described the secret of Radha and Krishna.

94I praise the wise Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya,
who is called Brihaspati, the guru of the gods.

95I shall praise King Prataparudra,
who was granted the sight of Mahaprabhu's six-armed form.76

96Having praised the feet of the brahmana Raghunatha Dasa,
[I praise] Vishnudasa the vaidya and Vipradasa of Utkala.77

97I praise Kanai Khutiya, a stream of the rasa of prema,
whose nature and feeling are like a gopi's;

98his sons are Jagannatha Dasa and Balarama:
what shall I say of their greatness? It is incomparable.

99I praise Jagannatha Dasa, a guru in the rasa of song:
at his songs the creepers and trees of the forest weep.

100I praise Balarama Dasa, the Oriya Vaishnava:
Jagannatha and Balarama are captive to his feeling.78

101Govindananda Thakura, called Sugriva,
built a great bridge for the Lord.79

102I praise Kashishvara, Simheshvara, Shivananda;
I praise with joy Sri Chandaneshvara.80

103I shall praise Madhava Pattanayaka;
I shall praise Hari Bhatta and Baladeva Mahati.

104I praise Subuddhi Mishra, who gives understanding to the unwise;
I praise Shrinatha Mishra, knower of the truth of Krishna.

[p. 52]

105I shall carefully praise Tulasi Mishra;
with body, word and mind I praise Kashinatha Mahati.81

106I shall praise Ramananda, the ornament of the Vasu family,
whose family are bees at Gaura's lotus feet.

107Purushottama Brahmachari and Sri Madhu Pandita,
two noble servants of Chaitanya, I praise.

108I praise the brahmana Ramachandra, Pandita Shrikara;
I praise Yadu Kavichandra, an ocean of happiness.82

109I shall praise Pandita Sri Dhananjaya,
whose renunciation is proclaimed in the world:

110giving at the Lord's feet a household worth a hundred thousand,
he took a pot in his hand and put on a kaupina.83

111I praise both feet of Pandita Suryadasa,
whose son-in-law Prabhu Nityananda became.

112I shall praise the feet of Thakura Vamshivadana,
who formerly was the flute at Krishna's lips.

113With care I shall praise Murari Chaitanya Dasa,
whose pastimes and play are with pythons.

114I praise Jagannatha Sena, Paramananda Gupta;
I shall praise the boy Ramadasa and Kavichandra.

115I shall praise Vallabhacharya, Sena Kamsari;
I shall praise Bhaskara — a descent of Vishvakarma.

116I praise Balarama Dasa, the teacher of song,
who has no business other than service to Nityananda.84

[p. 53]

117I praise Mahesha Pandita, maddened by Krishna;
I praise Jagadisha Pandita, who delights in dancing.

118I praise Narayani's son, Vrindavana Dasa,
whom all devotees call Vedavyasa.

119The Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata is his composition;
this book has enchanted the three worlds.85

120I shall praise the wise Krishnadasa of Behari,86
who lives in the village of Badagachhi:

121this man, in the net of love,
kept Nitaichand captive in his house.

122Pandita Thakura came and, striking his chest,
seized [Him] by the edge of His cloth and led Him away, saying: "My Lord!"

123In separation from Nityananda, Thakura Krishnadasa
spent seven months like a madman.

124Nityananda came again to his house,
and, gaining the sight of Nityananda, he grew calm.87

125I shall praise Paramananda, the best of avadhutas,
whose body is full of the rasa of prema.

126I praise Pandita Gangadasa, who lives at Anadi;88
I praise Yadunatha Dasa, sweet in his pastimes.

127I praise Purushottama Tirtha, Tirtha Sri Rama;
I praise Raghunatha Puri, [that] my heart's desire be fulfilled.89

128I praise Ashrama Upendra, Hariharananda;
I praise Tirtha Vasudeva, Puri Sri Ananta.90

[p. 54]

129I praise the sweet-formed Mukunda Kaviraja;
I praise Rajiva (?) Pandita in Navadvipa.91

130I praise Shishu Krishnadasa, the little cowherd,
whose body Nityananda nourished with His own hands.92

131Then I worshipped Madhava Acharya,
whose work it is always to describe Krishna's qualities:

132he composed the Krishna-mangala following the Bhagavata —
this song became known to the whole world.93

133Nrisimha Chaitanya Dasa and Krishnadasa —
two noble ones, an abode of love, I praise.

134I praise the utterly penniless Sri Shankara Ghosha,
with whose playing on the dampha the Lord is pleased.

135I praise Madhava Acharya, the jewel of the twice-born,
whose wife is Ganga, Nityananda's daughter.94

136I shall praise the feet of Ganga-devi,
Shivananda Chakravarti, Narayana Padiyari.95

Conclusion

137Here ends a brief Vaishnava-vandana:
the devotees of Chaitanya are countless — they cannot be numbered.

138And how many more hundreds and thousands of Vaishnavas
fill the three worlds!

139In the north, south, east and west
countless Vaishnavas have descended to earth.

140At the beginning of the age of Kali, at Chaitanya's descent,
by Chaitanya's mercy there are Vaishnavas in every house.

[p. 55]

141Therefore the Vaishnavas are without number:
freely wander all these purifiers of the fallen.

142The Lords of them all are Chaitanya and Nityananda:
these are the devotees of the two Mahaprabhus.

143Who can know the truth of the Vaishnavas?
The Sri Bhagavata proclaims the greatness of the Vaishnavas.

144Such a praise of the feet of all the Vaishnavas,
when read and heard, frees one from suffering.

145[One] is freed from sin, his body becomes pure;
by reading and hearing the heart becomes clear.

146On his lips shines the name "Krishna";
whatever he desires is fulfilled.

147In his throat the goddess Sarasvati plays;
Kamala comes and settles in his house.

148Wherever he goes, he knows no defeat:
everywhere he goes as a victor.

149Disease, old age and fever do not touch his body;
he is healthy and always content.

150Surely he will attain pure devotion —
with this longing it was composed by Vrindavana Dasa.96

Thus ends the "Vaishnava-vandana" composed by Sri Vrindavana Dasa.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Attribution. In the 1910 edition this vandana is the "Third" (the second is Devakinandana's, Pt. 2); the colophon ascribes it to Vrindavana Dasa. But the author himself praises "Narayani's son, Vrindavana Dasa", the author of the Chaitanya-bhagavata (vv. 17, 118–119), so he is not the author of CB. Majumdar calls him the "second Vrindavana Dasa" and regards the vandana as largely a retelling of the Sanskrit vandana of Pt. 1. Indeed, the order of names and many characterisations agree with Pt. 1 almost word for word; parallels are noted in the footnotes. Tripadi stanzas (two long lines of three parts each) and payar couplets are numbered consecutively; refrains are not numbered.
  2. A Sanskrit dedicatory verse. The word santau (সন্তৌ) is unclear.
  3. Vv. 2–5 are an introduction not found in Pts. 1 and 2. "Hare Krishna Rama" is the maha-mantra.
  4. Cf. Pt. 2, 3–5. "Janardana accepts the feeling": the Lord looks at the feeling, not at the words.
  5. An apology for breaking the order, as in Pt. 1, 6 and Pt. 2, 5.
  6. Cf. Pt. 1, 9–10; Pt. 2, 6–7.
  7. Cf. Pt. 1, 11; Pt. 2, 8.
  8. Cf. Pt. 1, 12 ("the second body of the Lord"); Pt. 2, 9.
  9. Cf. Pt. 1, 14–15; Pt. 2, 10–11.
  10. Cf. Pt. 1, 18 (Jahnavi is Ananga-manjari). According to GGD 65, Vasudha and Jahnavi are Varuni and Revati; GGD 66 gives both opinions on which of them is Ananga-manjari.
  11. Cf. Pt. 1, 22 ("Sri Chaitanya appearing a second time"); GGD 67: Virachandra is non-different from Chaitanya. The Lord's secret counsel with Nityananda at Nilachala is known only from this vandana.
  12. The Chaitanya-bhagavata says nothing about Virachandra: he was born after it was written. The author's reference is probably inexact. Abhirama — see vv. 69–72.
  13. Ganga, Nityananda's daughter, is the river Ganga herself, who came forth from Vishnu's foot (GGD 69). Brahma washed Vamana's foot with water from his vessel, and it became the Ganga. "Radha and Krishna in liquid form" and "Bhagavan become water" are traditional names of the Ganga (cf. Pt. 1, 24–25); no impersonal Brahman is meant.
  14. Cf. Pt. 1, 24–29; GGD 69 (Madhava is King Shantanu).
  15. Cf. Pt. 1, 30; Pt. 2, 14.
  16. Cf. Pt. 1, 31; Pt. 2, 15.
  17. Cf. Pt. 1, 32.
  18. Cf. Pt. 1, 33; Pt. 2, 16.
  19. Cf. Pt. 1, 36; Pt. 2, 17–18. GGD 90.
  20. Cf. Pt. 1, 36, 38; Pt. 2, 19–20. GGD 93–95.
  21. Cf. Pt. 1, 38–39. Jagadananda is "like Sarasvati in another form", as in Pt. 1, 38 ("another form of Vani"); according to GGD 51 he is a manifestation of Satyabhama. Paramananda is probably Paramananda Puri (cf. v. 42). Gopinatha is Gopinatha Acharya (Pt. 2, 21).
  22. Cf. Pt. 1, 39–40. GGD 91: Murari Gupta is Hanuman. The question mark after "as the moon" is the editor's.
  23. Cf. Pt. 1, 40–41; Pt. 2, 24–25.
  24. Cf. Pt. 1, 42; Pt. 2, 26.
  25. Cf. Pt. 1, 43; Pt. 2, 27–28.
  26. Cf. Pt. 1, 44; Pt. 2, 29.
  27. Cf. Pt. 1, 45; Pt. 2, 30.
  28. Cf. Pt. 1, 46; Pt. 2, 30.
  29. Six brahmacharis, as in Pt. 1, 47–48 (a fact known only from the vandanas).
  30. Cf. Pt. 1, 48–49; Pt. 2, 33–34. Shridhara sold banana-leaf cups, bananas and banana pith, and the Lord bargained with him (CB Adi 12; GGD 133).
  31. Cf. Pt. 1, 49–50; Pt. 2, 35–36.
  32. Cf. Pt. 1, 50, 52; Pt. 2, 37–38. "Garudai" is Garuda (Pandita).
